content: Ceftobiprole medocaril sodium should be administered intravenously at a dose of 3 mg/kg every 8 hours, with a maximum dose not exceeding 667 mg per administration. The treatment duration is typically 7 to 14 days. Ceftobiprole medocaril sodium, an inhibitor of OATP1B1/1B3 transporters, can increase the plasma concentrations of substrates of these transporters. This interaction may lead to elevated levels or enhanced effects of certain drugs, necessitating caution or alternative therapeutic strategies. Below are specific interactions: 1. Elagolix: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of elagolix. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Ambrisentan: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of ambrisentan. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Atorvastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of atorvastatin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Bosentan: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of bosentan. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Caspofungin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of caspofungin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Digoxin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of digoxin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Ezetimibe: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of ezetimibe. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Fexofenadine: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of fexofenadine. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Fluvastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of fluvastatin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Glyburide: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of glyburide. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Irinotecan: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of irinotecan. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Letermovir: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of letermovir. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Lovastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of lovastatin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Methotrexate: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of methotrexate. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Momelotinib: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of momelotinib. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Olmesartan: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of olmesartan. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Paclitaxel: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of paclitaxel. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Penicillin G Procaine: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of penicillin G procaine. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Pitavastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of pitavastatin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 22. Pravastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of pravastatin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Repaglinide: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of repaglinide. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Resmetirom: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Revefenacin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of revefenacin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Rifampin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of rifampin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Rosuvastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of rosuvastatin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Simvastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of simvastatin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of sulbactam/durlobactam. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Vadadustat: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of vadadustat. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Valsartan: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of valsartan. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Voxilaprevir: Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of voxilaprevir. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Zavegepant (Intranasal): Ceftobiprole increases the level or effect of zavegepant. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Ceftobiprole also increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of aminoglycosides such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, plazomicin, and tobramycin. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these agents. Ceftobiprole may reduce the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors, including atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, cosibelimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, and tislelizumab. Co-administration may interfere with their efficacy, and caution is advised. For drugs like atogepant and eluxadoline, ceftobiprole increases their levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. In summary, ceftobiprole medocaril sodium has significant drug interaction potential, particularly as an OATP1B1/1B3 inhibitor, and requires careful consideration of co-administered medications to avoid adverse effects or reduced therapeutic efficacy.
